title: reduce GPU memory and workspace: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: several production clusters observed OOMs and high workspace usage for long-context generations (8k+ tokens) on A100/RTX-class GPUs under mixed workloads. This PR reduces peak GPU memory and per-kernel workspace by combining selective activation checkpointing, a reuse-friendly scratch buffer arena allocator, and KV-cache packing/compaction. Approach: 1) Add selective activation checkpointing that targets large MLP and attention intermediate activations while leaving small ops uncheckpointed to minimize recompute overhead. 2) Introduce a global scratch buffer arena with per-stream sub-allocators and LRU reuse to avoid repeated cudaMallocs and reduce peak fragmentation. 3) Implement kernel workspace hints and fallbacks: kernels now expose preferred and minimal workspace profiles; at runtime the allocator picks a minimal-profile variant when workspace pressure is high. 4) KV-cache improvements: compact stored keys/values using dtype-aware packing and add asynchronous eviction/compaction to reclaim unused KV pages during long-running sessions. 5) Scheduler change: continuous-batching now communicates hard workspace budgets to the kernel scheduler to avoid overcommit; small reordering of batches favors latency-sensitive routes when memory pressure is detected. 6) Add runtime flags and per-deployment defaults so Dedicated/Private customers can tune checkpointing aggressiveness and arena sizes. Testing & validation: microbenchmarks across model families (causal LLaMA-like, encoder-decoder) show 18-35% reduction in peak GPU memory and up to 12% median latency regression in worst-case due to recompute (configurable) with end-to-end throughput parity in batch-friendly workloads. CI + cluster tests: unit tests, integration tests, and a small perf canary on staging with 64-concurrency were run. Rollout plan: opt-in feature gate for 2 weeks, then gradual default-on for Hosted and Dedicated with telemetry; provide rollback flag at runtime. Related: Linear ENG-2145, ENG-2188, PERF-333, incident INT-4578. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf microbenchmarks - [x] canary in staging - [x] docs/SDK flag updated (python/ts) Links: Linear/ENG-2145, ci/perf-canary runs, and internal design doc (design/doc/arena-checkpointing.md).

release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory by 18-35% via selective activation checkpointing, scratch buffer arena reuse, kernel workspace profiles, and KV-cache compaction. New runtime flags to tune aggressiveness. Opt-in for 2 weeks, then gradual rollout.
notes_for_ops: When rolling out, monitor runtime.metrics.gpu_peak_memory and runtime.metrics.kv_compaction_reclaimed_bytes; recommended default arena sizes: small=256MB, medium=1GB, large=4GB. If memory regressions observed, set REDWOOD_CHECKPOINTING_POLICY=conservative or disable arena with REDWOOD_RUNTIME_ARENA_ENABLE=false.
